molt.build.cost: The next build of each project is a full one rather than an incremental one.
molt.build.name: bin and obj folders
molt.build.what: Compiler output under every project in the folder you pick.
molt.description: Sheds the caches and build output that can be rebuilt, and says what losing each one costs before you do it.
molt.detail.bin: Recoverable from the Recycle Bin. Note that the room does not actually come back until the bin is emptied.
molt.detail.permanent: This cannot be undone. Everything here is rebuilt by the tool that made it, so the cost is time rather than data.
molt.dumps.cost: Nothing, unless you are in the middle of investigating a crash.
molt.dumps.name: Crash dumps
molt.dumps.what: Memory dumps written when something crashed.
molt.mode.bin: Sent to the Recycle Bin. Recoverable, but the room is not back until the bin is emptied.
molt.mode.permanent: Deleted outright. The room comes back immediately and nothing can be undone.
molt.note.excluded: Browser caches are left out on purpose: they are locked while the browser is running, so clearing them is unreliable. The JetBrains folder is left out too, because it holds settings and plugins as well as caches and telling them apart reliably is more than this should guess at.
molt.note.pickroot: Pick a projects folder above and bin and obj folders under it will be measured too.
molt.npm.cost: Nothing, beyond a slower first install.
molt.npm.name: npm cache
molt.npm.what: What npm keeps so it does not fetch the same tarball twice.
molt.nuget-http.cost: Nothing, beyond a slower first restore while they are fetched again.
molt.nuget-http.name: NuGet download cache
molt.nuget-http.what: Packages NuGet kept a copy of after downloading them.
molt.nuget-packages.cost: Every project has to download its packages again on the next restore. Safe, but not quick, and useless without an internet connection.
molt.nuget-packages.name: NuGet global packages
molt.nuget-packages.what: Every package version any project on this machine has ever restored.
molt.permanent: Delete outright instead of using the Recycle Bin
molt.pip.cost: Nothing, beyond a slower first install.
molt.pip.name: pip cache
molt.pip.what: Wheels pip kept after building or downloading them.
molt.status.left.bin: {0} sent to the Recycle Bin, {1} left behind
molt.temp.cost: Nothing. Anything touched in the last few days is left alone in case it is still in use.
molt.temp.name: Windows temp, older than {0} days
molt.temp.what: Scratch files programs wrote and did not clean up.
molt.title: What can be shed
molt.unity.cost: Unity reimports the whole project the next time it opens it, which on a large project is a long coffee.
molt.unity.name: Unity Library and Temp folders
molt.unity.what: What Unity imports every asset into so it does not have to do it again.
